findings.message: Dropping the `| None` here changes what /api/v2/monitor/health reports for a deployment that simply has no triggerer or no standalone dag processor: it used to be `null` ("component not deployed", and the old docs said so explicitly) and now it is `"unhealthy"`. Every probe or alert rule that keys off that string will start firing on deployments that were never running those components. If this is intentional it needs a newsfragment and a note in the 3.4 upgrade docs; otherwise please keep returning None when there are no job rows at all.

`end_date IS NULL` is not the same as "running" - a scheduler or triggerer killed by SIGKILL, OOM, or a pod eviction leaves a row with no end_date forever, and test_get_jobs_health_returns_unfinished_jobs_ordered_by_heartbeat locks that in by asserting a FAILED job is returned. Two consequences: `detailed_status` is pinned to "degraded" permanently after the first crash, which makes the new field useless as an alert signal; and this unbounded query plus the resulting `instances` array runs on every liveness/readiness probe, replacing what used to be a LIMIT 1. Please filter on `Job.state == JobState.RUNNING` too, and consider a cap on how many instances are returned.
